name: Powder / ombre / nano brows

lead: Powder, ombre and nano brows are salon names for semi-permanent brow tattoos that fill sparse or uneven brows with a soft, shaded finish that looks like brow makeup. The result is visible right after the session.

A machine places pigment, commonly iron-oxide based, into the upper skin layers with fine needles, rather than drawing single hair strokes by hand as in microblading. Powder and ombre styles are usually lighter at the front and darker toward the tail, and nano uses very fine needles for a subtler result. No studies specific to these styles were found, so what is known comes from general information on cosmetic tattooing.

paras: People book a salon session, pick a shade and shape, and return for touch-ups. Because the pigment sits shallow it fades over months to a couple of years. It suits people who like a defined, filled-in brow look without drawing it on each day.

Reported risks of cosmetic tattooing include infection, reactions to pigment, granulomas, pigment migration and colour change. In the US there is no federal regulation or standard for testing the ink, and rules vary elsewhere.

angle.text: These semi-permanent brow tattoos give a soft, shaded fill that looks like brow makeup, so brows look fuller and more defined from the moment the session ends. They are popular salon services and fade over months to a couple of years. No dedicated studies exist for these styles.

lead: Powder, ombre and nano brows are names used for semi-permanent cosmetic eyebrow tattooing in which pigment is deposited with a machine rather than drawn stroke by stroke by hand. Powder and ombre styles aim for a soft, shaded, make-up-like fill that is typically lighter at the front of the brow and darker toward the tail, while nano brows use very fine needles for a subtler result. These terms are trade and salon vocabulary rather than medical ones.

Related hand-applied microblading is described by Wikipedia as eyebrow tattooing in which individual hair-like strokes are made with a handheld tool, in contrast to the machine method used for most eyebrow tattoos [1]. The same article notes that pigment placed in the upper dermis fades faster than in conventional tattoos, that touch-ups are commonly recommended, and that risks include pigment migration, colour change, infection and granulomas [1]. No clinical studies specific to powder, ombre or nano techniques were found.
infobox: Varies by jurisdiction; not federally regulated in the US [1]

paras: Cosmetic eyebrow tattooing began as a medical camouflage procedure for hair loss of the brows (madarosis), and cosmetic versions spread in the 1980s and 1990s [1]. Salon names for brow-tattoo styles have multiplied since, with microblading becoming widely adopted in North America by the mid-2010s and names such as 3D brows also appearing [1]. Powder, ombre and nano brows are among the machine-based styles marketed as alternatives to hand-drawn strokes. Descriptions of exactly how each term differs are set by individual studios rather than by a standard definition.

Wikipedia reports that a microblading treatment may last up to two years, with a touch-up often recommended after about six weeks and again every 12 to 18 months, and that fading depends on pigment, sun exposure, skin type and skincare products [1]. Iron-oxide-based pigments in brown or black tones are the most common [1]. How these figures apply to machine-applied styles has not been established in published studies.

As with all tattooing, risks include bloodborne infections and reactions to pigment ingredients, and granulomas can form in treated skin [1]. Pigment can migrate, change colour or fade unevenly [1]. In the United States the practice is not regulated at the federal level and there is no standard for testing the ink, while in Canada regulation is by province [1].

Brow tattoos are discussed in appearance communities as a way to fill sparse or asymmetric brows, and sit alongside brow tinting and brow reshaping in grooming discussions. No community sources were reviewed for this entry, so specific claims are not documented here.

timeline.event: Cosmetic eyebrow tattooing spreads beyond its medical use for hair-loss camouflage. [1]
Microblading becomes widely adopted in the US and Canada. [1]
